meta.title: IPO-day reconciliation — can the marks reproduce the AUM? (no IPO add, no leverage)
meta.assumptions: SpaceX share count unchanged (no IPO add); no leverage (net = sum of marks); preferred tracks common proportionally; public basket proxied by the 23 hedge names.
meta.disclaimer: Analysis, not advice. Public-basket return is a proxy (covers ~92% of the 5/31 disclosed weights), which sets the error band on the implied-buy estimate.

conclusion: AUM grew +7.4% (19.0B->20.4B) but per-share NAV only +5.5% — the 1.9-point gap is ~$357M of net inflows, not an IPO buy. The +5.5% NAV is almost entirely the SpaceX re-mark (+5.0% on its own), and sits INSIDE the no-add prediction band (5.3%-5.8%). A material IPO purchase (>~$516M) would have lifted NAV above the band; it didn't. Implied add ~$-307M to $+228M ≈ 0 within proxy noise. So as of 2026-06-12 close there is no evidence Baron Partners/BPTIX added SpaceX at the IPO; the firm-wide $1B order more likely sits in the private BaronX vehicles or hasn't settled into this NAV yet.
